justifications.functional_suitability: Consultation, Prescription, AI Symptom Checker and Consent & Policy components cover R-01 to R-04, with Media Relay Containers for video. Gaps: no clinician-specific or scheduling component, and the consent per-purpose UI is only implied by Local State & Consent Manager.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Regional Redis Caches, SFU Media Router, adaptive-bitrate WebRTC, the Localization & Fallbandwidth component and GKE scaling support efficiency. Gaps: no asynchronous messaging, no explicit autoscaling or capacity targets, and Fallbandwidth is vague.
justifications.compatibility: REST and HL7 FHIR over mTLS to EU National e-Prescription Gateways and US Pharmacy Networks, plus OIDC/eIDAS/Login.gov identity providers. Gaps: no adapters per national standard, FHIR is also used for the EU, and no anti-corruption layer is shown.
justifications.usability: Web Application & Mobile App Containers serve patients and clinicians, with an offline-first Local State & Consent Manager and Offline Sync Queue. Gaps: no clinician-specific interface, no accessibility mechanism, and the Localization component is only vaguely described.
justifications.reliability: TURN/STUN Relay, Offline Sync Queue, adaptive bitrate and Cloud SQL regional instances support degraded operation. Gaps: no explicit HA, failover, backup or DR, no circuit breakers or retries, and no concrete 300 kbit/s audio-only fallback.
justifications.security: mTLS and Istio, Cloud KMS CMEK, VPC Service Controls, WORM Medical Artifact Buckets with AI trace bundles, the OPA-based Consent & Policy component, the API Gateway Auth Interceptor and PII stripping toward AI providers. Gaps: unclear residency enforcement for cross-region access and the audit log pipeline.
justifications.maintainability: Decomposed into microservices (Consultation, Prescription, AI Symptom Checker, Consent & Policy), with an API Gateway and mesh. Gaps: the BI Ingestion and Notification components have unclear coupling, the multi-language stack adds overhead, and all services sit in one GKE container.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes/GKE, Istio, PostgreSQL, Coturn and Mediasoup are portable open technologies, and the regions are separate. Gaps: heavy use of GCP-specific services (Cloud Endpoints, Memorystore, Cloud KMS, VPC Service Controls), with no abstraction layer or IaC.

sensitivity_points: No autoscaling stated for media relays
tradeoffs: Regional isolation limits pooling capacity versus residency
PERF-01.justification: Mediasoup SFU, Coturn and GKE are plausible for scale, but there is no autoscaling, capacity or join-time mechanism. The 10 s join target is unaddressed, so it is feasible with unaddressed risks.

tradeoffs: Third-party AI offers convenience but weakens latency and traceability control
PERF-02.justification: The synchronous call to an external AI provider through the egress filter has no caching, autoscaling or latency budget. 14 requests/s at under 3 s p95 is plausible but depends entirely on the provider, and the design is unclear about the client-side module role.

sensitivity_points: Adaptive bitrate and audio-only fallback not specified
tradeoffs: Offline caching of PHI improves resilience but increases device data risk
AVAIL-01.justification: Adaptive-bitrate WebRTC, an encrypted local store, an offline queue and a Fallbandwidth service support the scenario. Audio-only fallback and the notes-loss guarantee are not explicit, so some risk remains.

tradeoffs: Strict residency prevents failover to the EU, requiring in-US redundancy
AVAIL-02.justification: Only one region per jurisdiction is defined, with no second US region, replicas, backups or failover runbook. Residency is preserved, but restoring service within 1 hour is not supported by any stated mechanism.

sensitivity_points: Prescription service has no adapter abstraction
tradeoffs: A single Prescription service is simple but couples national standards
MOD-01.justification: Integration is isolated in the Prescription component, which limits the change to it. No per-country adapter or anti-corruption layer is defined, so confining changes to one adapter is not guaranteed and the service will probably need modification.

sensitivity_points: No model registry or rollback mechanism
tradeoffs: External model providers ease updates but reduce version control
MOD-02.justification: AI trace bundles in WORM buckets support traceability, but model versioning, registry, canary rollout and rollback are not defined. Third-party providers may change models without notice, so version linkage is unreliable.

tradeoffs: Strict regional isolation conflicts with cross-region clinical access
SEC-01.justification: OPA policy enforcement, consent injection and regional isolation provide a foundation, but no cross-region access flow, region-aware routing or denial logging path is shown. Audit logging exists through Cloud Logging and PostgreSQL audit logs, but a denied-request flow is unspecified.

sensitivity_points: Stale signed consent claims on clients
tradeoffs: Offline consent caching helps availability but delays revocation
SEC-02.justification: Consent is stored centrally and injected per request, which allows revocation within 24 hours. Enforcement in BI Ingestion and downstream research sharing is not explicit. Verification relies on audit logs, but claim expiry is unspecified.
